messages:

Cc: accounts-payable@heliotsystems.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood supplier setup — insurance & PO questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the onboarding checklist — we're ready to move forward. A couple quick questions so our AP team can raise the PO:

- What exact language should appear on the COI for Redwood (named insured / additional insured / waiver of subrogation)?
- Do you require a specific limits schedule (e.g. General Liability $1M/$2M, E&O $1M)?
- What's the timing for PO generation once we submit the COI and W9? Our AP is targeting net-45 payment terms; do you accept net-45 or only net-30?

I'm attaching the COI template we'll upload. If it's easier, a short checklist or example COI that meets your procurement rules would be great.

Appreciate it — Elena

Attachment: Heliot_W9_2027-05-18.pdf (PDF, 78KB)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Elena Morris <elena@heliotsystems.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood supplier setup — insurance & PO questions

Elena — thanks for sending these over. Quick answers inline below, plus next steps.

On Tue, May 18, 2027 at 09:12 AM Elena Morris <elena@heliotsystems.com> wrote:
> - What exact language should appear on the COI for Redwood (named insured / additional insured / waiver of subrogation)?

Our procurement standard for commercial vendor relationships (non-strategic SaaS supplier) is:
- Redwood Inference, Inc. listed as Certificate Holder AND Additional Insured on the General Liability line (Redwood Inference, Inc., 425 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94105).
- Waiver of subrogation requested but not mandatory for smaller suppliers — we'll accept "best efforts" language if carrier declines.

> - Do you require a specific limits schedule?

Preferred: General Liability 1,000,000 each occurrence / 2,000,000 aggregate; Professional Liability / E&O 1,000,000. Cyber insurance is required if any vendor will handle customer data — Heliot please confirm scope. If you are only providing internal tooling with no customer data, cyber may be optional.

> - What's the timing for PO generation once we submit the COI and W9? Our AP is targeting net-45 payment terms; do you accept net-45 or only net-30?

Procurement note (cc'ing Ben): once we have the signed COI and a completed W9, Procurement typically issues a conditional PO within 48 business hours and finalizes terms after validation. Standard Redwood terms are net-30; we can evaluate net-45 for larger volume deals but will need approval from Finance (Ben, can you flag if we can make an exception here?).

Next steps:
- Elena, confirm whether Heliot will be additional insured and whether cyber cover is present.
- Heliot: if COI carrier requires a specific addendum, upload to vendor portal and we'll review.

I'll forward this to Ben to kick off PO creation once you confirm.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Vendor Operations Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachment references: we pulled the COI and W9 you attached and saved to the intake ticket.

Kimberly — thanks for the clear breakdown. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can add Redwood as Additional Insured on General Liability; waiver language will depend on the primary carrier but we'll request it.
- Our broker confirms we have GL 1M/2M and E&O 1M. Cyber: Heliot will not access customer PII or logs, so we do not carry cyber for this product. Should we still provide an attestation?
- Net-45 is preferred by our AP. Would Redwood consider a one-time net-45 pilot for the first 90 days and then revert to net-30, or is that problematic?

We've uploaded the signed COI and W9 to your vendor intake portal just now (see attachments in original). Please confirm receipt and whether the absence of cyber insurance is an automatic blocker or if an attestation is sufficient for this scope.

Best,
Procurement Team
Heliot Systems

Kimberly / Elena — looping in Procurement next steps.

Thanks for the uploads, team. Summary and proposed path:
- COI: acceptable as submitted (Redwood listed as Additional Insured / Certificate Holder). We'll note waiver-of-subrogation as "requested" and mark it as conditional acceptance.
- Cyber absence: for a vendor that does not handle customer data, we accept a signed attestation confirming no access to customer PII/logs. Elena — can you provide a single-paragraph attestation on company letterhead? That will satisfy our risk team and allow PO issuance.
- PO & terms: We can issue a conditional PO (PO-8072) with net-45 for the first 90 days as a pilot, after which standard net-30 will apply unless escalated. The conditional PO will include the attestation clause and a pass/fail review at the 90-day mark.

Action items:
1) Elena: upload a one-paragraph attestation on letterhead to the vendor portal (or send to accounts-payable).
2) Kimberly: please create PO-8072 as a conditional PO and share DocuSign link so Heliot can accept.
3) Marissa: please confirm whether there are any billing exceptions we should capture for AP.

I'll open the PO and put the conditional terms in the DocuSign envelope. Linking the draft: https://app.docusign.com/heliot/po-acceptance-8072

Ben Carter
Senior Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference
